exact_prompt: Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: a transparent photographic cutout for a very small sign fastened flush to the old stone gate pillar of Abraza tu Paz, a deeply shaded Mediterranean garden with olive-green foliage, weathered warm-grey sandstone, bougainvillea and patches of warm afternoon sun. Primary request: ONE small, plain, narrow VERTICAL weathered wooden plank, approximately 2:3 portrait proportion, almost straight front-facing view. Two tiny dark, hand-forged, aged iron nail heads are visibly driven into the wood: one near the top center and one near the bottom center, as if the board is nailed directly flat against stone. Fine, natural vertical wood grain, a few tiny worn splits at the edges, understated softened corners, thin real thickness visible only very subtly at right and bottom edges. Color muted medium weathered umber, warm grey-brown wood with a slight mossy olive cast, NOT bright orange, NOT fresh pale timber. Lighting is low-key soft garden shade, a subtle dapple of warm natural light near the upper-left corner and gentle darker shading at lower-right. The middle 70% of the front must be smooth enough for an HTML handwritten label and COMPLETELY BLANK. Composition: 2:3 portrait canvas, centered object fills about 90% of width and height with small clear transparent margins, real alpha around every contour, no scene behind it. Constraints: absolutely NO rope, no cord, no hanging loop, no chain, no posts, no frame, no decorative ornaments, no stone wall, no leaves, no letters, no text, no logos, no watermark, no background. Avoid rustic shop-sign kitsch and glossy varnish. It should be a quiet, humble, believable piece of old wood nailed to an existing garden entrance, not a UI card or a product advertising photo.
purpose: Reversible wood entrance sign experiment, two iron nails, no rope; handwritten text is overlaid in HTML
changes: PNG original preserved. WebP 768px wide, alpha preserved. Paper variant left intact.
